narrative:
The model determined that you have a 42% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

Three pieces of information about you weighed most heavily in this decision. First, your credit history of critical or other existing credits was the strongest factor. While this history actually pulled the prediction slightly toward approval, it was not enough to overcome the other risks. Second, the size of the loan you requested—4,249 DM—was the next most important driver. This amount is noticeably higher than the average of about 3,020 DM that approved applicants typically request, and it pushed the prediction toward denial. Third, the status of your checking account (0–200 DM) was the third strongest influence. Only 18% of approved applicants have a similar balance, while most hold no checking account at all; this limited balance worked against you and increased the perceived risk.

Taken together, the larger loan size and modest checking-account balance created enough concern to outweigh the somewhat reassuring aspects of your credit history, leading to the final decision.

You should focus on building a stronger financial profile before reapplying. Paying down existing debts, saving so you can request a smaller loan amount, and maintaining a healthier checking-account balance for several months will improve your prospects. Consider speaking with a financial advisor to create a clear plan.
